comparator.name: Art History
comparator.academicYear: Prospective entry-cohort sequence: 2027–2028 first year, 2028–2029 second year, 2029–2030 third year; checked 2026-09-25 against adopted 2026–2027 OER
comparator.route: Kunstgeschiedenis, standard route without study abroad, two permitted minors
comparator.sourceNotes: The public prospective pages explicitly form a single three-year entry-cohort sequence, 60+60+60 EC. Year one has twelve compulsory 5-EC courses; the 0-EC mentorship and RADAr elements do not contribute credit. Year two has 30 EC specified major courses and 30 EC of two restricted 15-EC Arts minors, whose individual courses are not imposed on all students. Year three without study abroad has Florence 10, American Art 5, Kunstwerelden 5, research work 10 and genuine free space 30 EC. The formally adopted 2026–27 OER describes a different current-cohort year-three list, including the exact same Paris course code also listed in its year two, and a career course rather than the later prospective Kunstwerelden. That cross-cohort single-year regulation is not combined as if both Paris instances could earn credit in one three-year route. The prospective sequence is provisional and future offerings may change; the 2026–27 OER confirms the current first-year field and broad 60/30+30/30+30 structure but is not represented as adopting the future year-three Florence list.

routeSelection.route: Kunstgeschiedenis, standard route without study abroad, two permitted minors
routeSelection.basis: The target is the generic Art History bachelor. The standard non-abroad route preserves the explicitly credited art-historical research and 30 EC open elective space; the two 15-EC permitted minors remain restricted choices. This is the coherent prospective three-year route shown to entrants and avoids double-counting the Paris excursion across two cohorts in the 2026–27 OER.

alternatives.label: Art history and visual culture
alternatives.concept: Historical study of artworks and archaeological objects across Europe, Africa and the Mediterranean joins aesthetics, museums, visual media and methods of researched cultural interpretation. UCR offers selective world regions and periods, not Radboud’s complete architecture and art-history survey, excursions or an art-history thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The 24-course curriculum sustains art history and visual culture through named art, methods and related courses.
progression: Every formal prerequisite precedes its dependent course, every assignment is offered in the stated term, and mandatory PPD falls in the first year; art-history survey and archaeological foundations support later specialist study.

alternatives.label: Heritage, identity and cultural power
alternatives.concept: Art and archaeological heritage provide the anchor for sustained inquiry into imperial collections, cultural ownership, Indigenous histories, rights, race and the public interpretation of objects. This programme gives more weight to political and social inquiry than the standard Art History curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The 24-course curriculum sustains heritage, identity and cultural power through named art, methods and related courses.
progression: Every formal prerequisite precedes its dependent course, every assignment is offered in the stated term, and mandatory PPD falls in the first year; art-history survey and archaeological foundations support later specialist study.
alternatives.distinctness: This route changes 5 courses (37.5 EC) against prior alternatives. It shifts from art and media survey toward a sustained political, legal and social inquiry into heritage.

alternatives.label: Art, visual media and environmental change
alternatives.concept: Art-history and heritage courses combine with visual-media interpretation, climate rhetoric, environmental science and landscape design. The environmental courses explain material and ecological processes depicted or contested in art and media; this is an interdisciplinary direction, not an art-history specialisation.

alternatives.distinctness: This route changes 8 courses (60.0 EC), 9 courses (67.5 EC) against prior alternatives. It adds a climate, ecology, landscape and environmental-communication sequence to visual arts and media.

candidates.label: Architecture in Asia and the Americas
candidates.reason: The selected closest route includes art-historical and archaeological global comparisons, but the catalogue has no dedicated Asian or American architecture survey or advanced architectural history sequence to anchor a distinct 24-course architecture degree.

selection.assessment: Three distinct feasible curricula represent the core, heritage-and-identity, and art-and-environment concepts. A further architecture-specific branch was assessed but lacks a specialist UCR sequence. Individual illustrative Florence and Paris excursions and downstream careers do not generate separate bachelor alternatives.

notes.text: The comparator is the coherent prospective 2027–30 entry-cohort plan, subject to change; the adopted 2026–27 OER differs in year three and lists Paris for both its concurrent second- and third-year cohorts. The comparison does not count the same excursion twice. UCR art-history, heritage and environmental-media curricula are interdisciplinary and do not replace the specialist Radboud architecture, Asian or American art sequences or its thesis.
